subject.title: Feature: Tool-level sandbox mode for selective isolation

question: Should OpenClaw add a core per-tool execution-placement contract for host versus sandbox routing, and should the source of truth be operator config, tool/plugin declarations, or a precedence-controlled combination?
rationale: The requested change creates new config and runtime semantics for a sandbox security boundary, so automation should not choose the permanent schema or host-escape model.

options.title: Design Core Placement Contract
options.body: Define a narrow schema and runtime decision point that keeps placement, filtering, browser behavior, web_fetch behavior, gateway-owned tools, and elevated exec explicitly separate.

options.title: Keep Session-Scoped Sandbox Model
options.body: Reject per-tool placement for now and document the intended model as session sandboxing plus elevated exec and sandbox tool policy filtering.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Sandbox Program
options.body: Use the broader sandbox architecture tracker as the design home while preserving this issue as the per-tool placement acceptance case.

recommendation.title: Design Core Placement Contract
recommendation.body: Define a narrow schema and runtime decision point that keeps placement, filtering, browser behavior, web_fetch behavior, gateway-owned tools, and elevated exec explicitly separate.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined signal from the live issue review and recent sandbox documentation/history around this boundary.
